RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-E288D08833-89297
Member: Riley Grant, Member ID W510384895
Date of notice: 2026-08-04
Requested service: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 (anterior cervical discectomy and fusion) described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04, reference number POC-E288D08833-89297. That notice states the reason for denial as follows: "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed, or in the alternative that I be provided the specific clinical criteria applied so that I may respond to them point by point.

1. The denial notice does not identify the specific medical-necessity criteria applied to my case.

The notice cites only a general reference to "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" without naming the document, policy number, or specific criteria used. In researching this appeal, I was unable to independently confirm which criteria set governs my case. I understand that Telligen, Inc., which performs utilization review for Idaho Medicaid, has publicly stated: "All cases must meet Idaho Medicaid criteria before applying any other criteria. Telligen uses MCG criteria." I was not able to obtain the text of either the "Idaho Medicaid criteria" or the MCG guideline itself, as neither is publicly published. Separately, I located a UnitedHealthcare Community Plan document titled "Spinal Fusion and Decompression (for Idaho Only)," Policy Number CS365ID.D, Effective Date June 1, 2026, which states that it "only applies to the state of Idaho, including Idaho Medicaid Plus plans," and that "Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Decompression +/- Fusion, Cervical … Fusion, Cervical Spine …" I am not certain whether this UnitedHealthcare document is the operative policy for my specific coverage category, and I did not obtain the underlying InterQual criteria text itself, as it is not publicly published either.

Given this, I formally request, pursuant to my appeal rights, that the plan/Telligen/Idaho Medicaid provide me in writing: (a) the exact name, policy number, and effective date of the medical-necessity criteria applied to deny CPT 22551 in my case; and (b) the specific criterion or criteria my clinical record was found not to satisfy. Without this information I am unable to know precisely which elements of my record the reviewer found lacking, but I address below the clinical elements that I understand are generally relevant to a request of this kind, based on my own understanding rather than any quoted plan language.

2. My clinical record documents the elements generally relevant to medical necessity for ACDF.

The following is a summary of my clinical history, in my own words, mapped to the categories I believe a reviewer would consider relevant to this determination. This is not a quotation of any plan document — I am stating this on my own behalf because I could not obtain the plan's specific bulleted criteria for cervical fusion:

- Symptom duration and chronicity: I have had 12 months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- Radicular symptoms and functional impact: I have radicular pain and numbness radiating into my right thumb and index finger, accompanied by weakness.
- Physical examination findings: My treating surgeon documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.
- Imaging confirmation: An MRI of my cervical spine performed 2026-06-24 showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression — a finding that corresponds anatomically to my clinical symptoms and exam findings.
- Conservative treatment already attempted and failed:
  - Supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, for 8 weeks (2026-05-17 through 2026-07-12), with 16 visits completed, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
  - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-26 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- Absence of contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

I believe this record reflects a chronic, imaging-confirmed, single-level cervical radiculopathy that has not responded to a substantial trial of non-surgical care, which I understand is generally the type of clinical picture that supports surgical intervention of this kind. However, because the plan has not quoted or provided me its specific criteria, I cannot confirm point-by-point compliance, and I ask that the reviewer do so explicitly in response to this appeal.

3. Documentation submitted with this appeal.

In support of this appeal, I am submitting (or asking my surgeon's office to submit on my behalf):
- The physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-17 through 2026-07-12 (16 visits).
- Records of NSAID trial and the 2026-05-26 corticosteroid injection, including documented duration of relief.
- The MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-24.
- Dr. Lindqvist's clinic notes documenting exam findings, including provocative testing and the neurologic deficit at the corresponding level.
- [Any additional records the plan specifies as necessary — not stated in the notice provided to me]

4. Request for peer-to-peer review and full policy citation.

I request a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Lindqvist and the physician reviewer who denied this request, as referenced in Telligen's own review process. I also renew my request, described above, that the plan identify — in writing, with policy title, number, and effective date — the specific medical-necessity criteria applied to CPT 22551 in my case, and the specific criterion the reviewer found unmet.

5. Appeal deadline.

The notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (by 2027-01-31). Because I have found public information suggesting that Idaho Medicaid fair-hearing deadlines for benefit denials may in some circumstances be shorter than 180 days, I am submitting this appeal now, well in advance of both the 180-day date stated in the notice and any shorter deadline that may apply, in order to preserve my appeal rights. I ask that the plan confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and confirm the applicable deadline for any further hearing rights.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or to schedule a peer-to-peer review. I have attached the clinical documentation referenced above.

Sincerely,

Riley Grant
Member ID: W510384895

Enclosures:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-17 to 2026-07-12)
